name: Paris

attributes.attribute: linked to the French city name
name may come from the Parisi tribe

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Paris is a figure in a Welsh story, the tale of Kulhwch and Olwen. He was king of the region that is now the French capital. Scholars reject the idea of a real king Paris. They trace the city name to the local Celtic tribe, the Parisi. That tribe also lived in the Yorkshire region of Britain. Another legend links Paris to the sunken city Ys. The name par-Ys carried a false meaning. A tale said Ys was drowned and Paris was a reflection of it.

okr.objective: Describe Paris as a figure in Welsh and Breton legend.
key_results: Paris appears as a king in the tale of Kulhwch and Olwen.
Scholars tie the city name to the Parisi tribe of Britain.
One legend links Paris to the sunken city of Ys.
